newsitem.title: USA: TENNESSEE JUDGE SETS HEARING IN INCORPORATION CASE.
newsitem.headline: TENNESSEE JUDGE SETS HEARING IN INCORPORATION CASE.

text.p: A Tennessee chancellor has scheduled a full hearing Sept 8 in a lawsuit challenging the constitutionality of a law that eased restrictions on incorporation of towns, the Commercial Appeal said Wednesday.
The action by Davidson County Chancllor Irwin Kilcrease Jr. eliminates the need for a hearing that had been set for Thursday to extend a temporary ban on incorporations and annexations.
By agreement of the parties, the temporary restraining order will remain in effect until Kilcrease issues a final ruling.

"I think that's a good sign," said Joe Sweat, executive director of the Tennessee Municipal League. "I don't think they would have agreed to delay it unless they were concerned about some constitutional issues."
Tennessee Municipal League, Memphis and four other cities filed suit against state and local elections officials after the new law sparked a rush of petitions for incorporation referendums.

Under the new law that took effect in April, only 225 residents are needed to form a new community and new towns can spring up on the border of existing towns. The law also gives incorporation of new towns priority over annexation attempts by neighboring towns.
City officials said the law threatens the right of towns to grow and could weaken tax revenue streams in existing municipalities.
In an analysis of the new law on Tuesday, Standard & Poor's Corp said it could hurt the credit quality of some mature cities in Tennessee.
